name: Balbach Teaching Dimension of Repeated-Coordinate Cubes
proof: For every $n\ge1$, an ordinary teacher must query each of the $n-1$ nonrepeated bits and at least one copy of the repeated bit. Otherwise the concept obtained by flipping an unqueried underlying bit is still consistent. Those $n$ queries suffice, so every target has ordinary minimum teaching size $n$. For any sample of size at most $n$, the initial Balbach filter retains every consistent concept, since all their thresholds equal $n$. No sample of size below $n$ can therefore teach its target, whereas its ordinary size-$n$ sample does. The uniform initial vector is fixed, proving BTD $n$ despite the repeated coordinates.
